items.prompt: White to move. Black's knight has just jumped from f6 to h5. Find White's best reply.

claims.statement: Bxe7 is the engine's top move; the other tries are clearly worse (depth 16).
One black piece attacks the bishop on h4 (the bishop on e7).
No white piece guards the bishop on h4.

hints: Which black piece now attacks the bishop on h4, and what guards it?
The bishop on e7 attacks h4 along the diagonal the knight just opened, and nothing defends h4. Can White remove the attacker?
The bishop takes on e7 first.
items.explain: The knight left f6, so the bishop on e7 attacks the bishop on h4, which nothing guards. White takes the attacker first with the bishop; the queen retakes and the trade has cost White nothing. The engine ranks the capture first at depth 16, ahead of the alternatives. It is the same unmasking idea as in the tactics lesson.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's pawn on g4 is defended by the rook and threatens to advance to g5. Find the move that does not ignore this plan.

claims.statement: Re8 is within 0.4 pawns of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
The pawn on g4 attacks f5 and h5.
The game move b5 is at least 0.7 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Where will the pawn on g4 go next, and what will it attack when it gets there?
The pawn can advance to g5 and attack the knight on f6. Which moves prepare for that, or take away squares from the pawns?
Re8 (a developing move) is the least bad: White stays slightly better, but the king is not weakened. g6 is worse.
items.explain: The pawn on g4 will advance to g5 and attack the knight on f6, so Black needs a move that deals with the storm or at least does not weaken the king. The engine prefers the rook move, though White stays slightly better (depth 16). In the game Black played ...b5, which does nothing about g5 and is rated about a pawn worse.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's king stands on e7 and the queen on g7 is already deep in his camp. Find the move that keeps the attack going.

claims.statement: Ng6+ is the engine's top move by a wide margin (depth 16).
The knight can go from f4 to g6 with check.

hints: Which White pieces can still give check?
The knight on f4 can check from g6. Look at what the queen on g7 attacks once the king has to move.
The knight to g6, check.
items.explain: The knight on f4 gives check on g6, forcing the king to move and bringing a new piece into the attack. The engine puts the move far ahead of the alternatives (depth 16); the game ended with this check.

items.prompt: White to move. Both sides have finished developing. Find the pawn move that challenges Black's centre.

claims.statement: e4 is the engine's top move (depth 16).
The pawn can go from e3 to e4.

hints: Which pawn stands in front of Black's central pawn on d5?
Black's pawn on d5 is supported by the pawn on c6. What could attack it again?
The pawn from e3 to e4 challenges d5.
items.explain: The pawn on e3 can advance to e4 and attack d5, which opens the e-file for the rooks. White has prepared the break with Rfe1, Rad1 and Bd3. The engine ranks the break first at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. The black king has taken on f7 and stands in front of its queen. Find the quiet follow-up.

claims.statement: Nc5 is the engine's top move by a wide margin (depth 16).
After Nc5 the knight attacks the bishop on b7 and the knight on e6.

hints: Which black pieces stand on e6 and b7, and which White piece could attack both?
A knight on c5 attacks the knight on e6 and the bishop on b7. What can Black take it with?
The knight to c5.
items.explain: The knight goes to c5 and attacks the knight on e6 and the bishop on b7 at once. Black can take it with the b-pawn, but then the rook takes the knight on e6 with the queen attacked, and after the queen retakes the white queen takes the bishop on b7 with check (the next board shows the line). The engine ranks Nc5 far above the alternatives (depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move. The bishop on h4 has no defender, and Black's own knight stands on f6 between the bishop on e7 and the target. Find the knight move that uncovers the attack.

claims.statement: Ng4 is the engine's top move (depth 16).
No white piece guards the bishop on h4.

hints: Which black piece would attack the bishop on h4 if the knight on f6 were not there?
The bishop on e7 looks along e7-f6-g5-h4. Where can the knight go with a threat of its own?
The knight to g4 attacks e3 and uncovers the bishop.
items.explain: The bishop on e7 attacks h4 as soon as the knight leaves f6, and nothing defends h4. The knight jumps to g4, where it attacks the pawn on e3 and the bishop on h4 is attacked at the same time. The engine ranks the jump first at depth 16, ahead of the quiet moves.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's knight has just jumped to g4 and the bishop on h4 is attacked by the bishop on e7. Find the capture that removes the attacker.

claims.statement: One black piece (the bishop on e7) attacks the bishop on h4.
Bxe7 is within 0.4 pawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).
After Bxe7 Qxe7 the engine still prefers Black slightly: between -110 and 40 centipawns from White's side.

hints: Which white pieces does the knight on g4 attack, and which does the bishop on e7 attack?
The bishop on e7 attacks h4 and the knight on g4 attacks e3. Which attacker can White remove with a capture of its own?
The bishop takes on e7.
items.explain: The bishop on h4 is attacked by the bishop on e7, and the knight on g4 attacks e3. Taking the attacker first removes the threat to h4; after the queen retakes, White can still take the knight. The game move fxg4 let Black take the bishop first and damaged White's pawns. Both captures leave Black slightly better, so the point is the habit: a loose bishop gave Black the choice.

feedback_by_move.f3g4: The game move. After ...Bxh4 White's pawns on e3, g2 and g4 are weak, and Black is slightly better.

items.prompt: Black to move after White has played g4. Which reply is a mistake: the knight on h5 back to f6, or the knight on d7 to e5?

claims.statement: Ne5 loses at least a piece compared with the best move (depth 16).
The retreat Nhf6 is the engine's top move (depth 16).

hints: Is the knight on h5 attacked? What would happen to it if Black ignores that?
If the knight on d7 jumps away, who takes the knight on h5?
Ne5 ignores the attack on h5, and the pawn takes the knight.
items.explain: The pawn on g4 attacks the knight on h5. The retreat to f6 saves the knight and attacks g4 in turn. The jump Ne5 leaves the knight on h5 attacked, and White wins a piece.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has just played ...Ng4. One of White's two bishops is loose (attacked, and no white piece guards it). Which one: the bishop on h4 or the bishop on d3?

claims.statement: One black piece attacks the bishop on h4.
No white piece guards the bishop on h4.
No black piece attacks the bishop on d3.

hints: For each bishop, count the black pieces that attack it and the white pieces that guard it.
Look along the diagonal from e7: where does it end?
The bishop on h4 is attacked by the bishop on e7 and nothing guards it.
items.explain: The bishop on e7 now looks along the diagonal to h4, because the knight left f6, and no white piece guards h4. The bishop on d3 is not attacked at all. A loose piece is one that is attacked and unguarded.
